_comment: The ORIGINAL identification signatures from the final-block review appendix,
These are the PRE-EDIT stems and option texts, with the plain-text export flattening
preserved, so the test suite can re-derive the id map by full content match rather

Q1.stem: An electron enters a region with an electric field E pointing downward and a magnetic field B pointing into the page. The electron moves to the right. For it to travel in a straight line without deflection, the field magnitudes must satisfy:

Q2.stem: A half-wave rectifier converts an AC input into a DC output by:
options: Allowing both positive and negative half-cycles to pass through
Allowing only one half-cycle (positive or negative) to pass while blocking the other
Doubling the frequency of the input signal
Inverting the negative half-cycle to produce a smooth constant voltage

Q3.stem: The depletion region at a PN junction forms because:
options: External voltage is applied to the junction
Majority carriers diffuse across the junction, leaving behind immobile ionized dopant atoms
Photons are absorbed at the junction, creating electron-hole pairs
The temperature gradient across the junction drives carriers apart

Q4.stem: The Bernoulli equation for an ideal fluid flowing in a horizontal pipe states that the sum of which quantities remains constant along a streamline?
options: Pressure energy, kinetic energy, and thermal energy
Static pressure, dynamic pressure (1/2 ρ v2), and hydrostatic pressure (ρ g h)
Pressure, velocity, and viscous shear stress
Gravitational potential energy, surface tension energy, and kinetic energy

Q5.stem: A cyclotron cannot accelerate neutrons because:
options: Neutrons are too heavy to reach relativistic speeds
Neutrons have no electric charge and cannot be deflected by magnetic or accelerated by electric fields
Neutrons decay too quickly to complete a full revolution
The magnetic field of a cyclotron repels neutral particles

Q6.stem: A positive charge moves to the right in a magnetic field directed into the page. The Lorentz force on the charge is directed:
options: Upward (toward the top of the page)
Downward (toward the bottom of the page)

Q7.stem: A perfect black body is an object that:
options: Absorbs all incident radiation but emits none
Absorbs all incident radiation and is also the most efficient emitter of thermal radiation
Emits radiation only at a single specific wavelength

Q8.stem: According to Wien's displacement law, as the temperature of a black body increases, the wavelength at which it emits maximum radiation:
options: Increases (shifts toward longer wavelengths / red shift)
Decreases (shifts toward shorter wavelengths / blue shift)
First increases then decreases as temperature rises

Q9.stem: The activity of a radioactive sample as a function of time follows which mathematical relationship?
options: Exponential decrease: A(t) = A0 e^(-λ t)

Q10.stem: A radioactive isotope has a decay constant of λ = 0.0693 per day. Its half-life is approximately:

Q11.stem: A substance is described as isotropic. This means that its physical properties are:
options: Dependent on the temperature but not direction
Uniform only along one specific crystal axis

Q12.stem: An ideal gas with adiabatic index γ = 5/3 is compressed adiabatically from volume 8 L to 1 L. If the initial pressure is 100 kPa, what is the final pressure?

Q13.stem: In an adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The gas absorbs heat from the surroundings and cools down
The temperature of the gas decreases because it does work at the expense of internal energy
The temperature remains constant because no heat is exchanged
The internal energy increases because no heat is lost

Q14.stem: A 2 kg mass oscillates on a spring with spring constant k = 800 N/m. What is the period of oscillation?

Q15.stem: A simple pendulum has a period of 2 seconds on Earth (g = 10 m/s2). What is the length of the pendulum?

Q16.stem: In simple harmonic motion, at which position is the kinetic energy of the oscillator at its maximum?
options: Kinetic energy is constant throughout the motion

Q17.stem: A soap bubble has a radius of 5 cm. If the surface tension of the soap solution is 0.04 N/m, what is the excess pressure inside the bubble compared to outside?

Q18.stem: Water (surface tension 0.073 N/m, density 1000 kg/m3, contact angle 0°) rises in a glass capillary tube to a height of 3 cm. What is the approximate inner radius of the tube? (g = 10 m/s2)

Q19.stem: A solenoid has 2000 turns wound uniformly over a length of 0.4 m and carries a current of 3 A. What is the magnetic field inside the solenoid? (μ0 = 4π × 10−7 T·m/A)

Q20.stem: A solenoid produces a magnetic field of 10 mT when carrying 2 A. If the current is increased to 5 A (with no other changes), the magnetic field becomes:

Q21.stem: Light of wavelength 310 nm strikes a metal surface with work function W = 3.0 eV. What is the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons? (Use E(eV) = 1240/λ(nm))

Q22.stem: In the photoelectric effect, if the intensity of light (above threshold frequency) is doubled while keeping the frequency unchanged, what happens?
options: The maximum kinetic energy of electrons doubles
The number of emitted electrons doubles but their maximum kinetic energy stays the same
Both the number and maximum kinetic energy of electrons double

Q23.stem: A muon has a half-life of 1.5 μs in its own rest frame. If it travels at 0.6c relative to Earth, what is its half-life as measured by an Earth observer?

Q24.stem: How much energy is released if 1 gram of matter is completely converted to energy? (c = 3 × 108 m/s)

Q25.stem: A uniform 4 m beam of negligible weight is supported at its center. A 40 N weight hangs 1.5 m to the left of the fulcrum. How far to the right of the fulcrum should a 60 N weight be placed to balance the beam?

Q26.stem: A 60 kg adult sits 1.5 m from the fulcrum of a seesaw. At what distance from the fulcrum should a 30 kg child sit to balance the seesaw? (g = 10 m/s2)

Q27.stem: How long must a current of 10 A flow through a solution of AgNO3 to deposit 5.4 g of silver? (MAg = 108 g/mol, z = 1, F = 96500 C/mol)

Q28.stem: The same quantity of electric charge is passed through solutions of CuSO4 and AgNO3 connected in series. If 2.16 g of silver is deposited, how much copper is deposited? (MAg = 108, zAg = 1; MCu = 64, zCu = 2)

Q29.stem: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 400 V. What is its de Broglie wavelength? (Use the shortcut: λ(nm) = 1.226/√V for electrons)

Q30.stem: An X-ray tube operates at 40 kV. What is the shortest wavelength X-ray it can produce? (Use: λmin(nm) = 1.240/V(kV))

Q31.stem: A 10 μF capacitor is connected to a 50 Hz AC source with peak voltage V0 = 100 V. What is the capacitive reactance and the peak current?

Q32.stem: At 25 degrees C, the saturation vapor pressure of water is 3.17 kPa. If the actual water vapor pressure in the air is 1.90 kPa, what is the relative humidity?

Q33.stem: What happens when air is cooled below its dew point temperature?
options: Water vapor condenses into liquid droplets

Q34.stem: Two long parallel wires are 0.2 m apart, each carrying a current of 5 A in the same direction. What is the force per unit length between them?

Q35.stem: The SI unit ampere was historically defined using which physical setup?
options: Force between two parallel current-carrying conductors
Deflection of an electron in a magnetic field
EMF produced by a changing magnetic flux

Q36.stem: A straight conductor of length 0.4 m moves at 3 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. What EMF is induced across its ends?

Q37.stem: The mass of a helium-4 nucleus is 4.0026 u, while the total mass of 2 free protons and 2 free neutrons is 4.0320 u. What does this mass difference represent?
options: Energy absorbed when the nucleus formed
Mass converted to nuclear binding energy via E = mc²
Energy lost to radiation during measurement

Q38.stem: Which nucleus has the highest binding energy per nucleon and is therefore the most stable?

Q39.stem: In a nuclear fission reactor, what is the primary function of the moderator?
options: To absorb excess neutrons and prevent supercriticality
To slow fast neutrons to thermal speeds so they can trigger further fission
To shield workers from γ radiation
To cool the reactor core and prevent overheating

Q40.stem: Which material is most effective at shielding against neutron radiation?

Q41.stem: A specific nuclear species defined by its atomic number Z and mass number A is called a:
